item_1.notes:
[chunk 1/2] SIFI-MATERIAL EXTRACTION FROM BROADCOM 10-K (2024). Key findings: (1) CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION: Top 5 end customers = 40% of FY2024 revenue (vs. 35% FY2023). This represents ELEVATED risk (severity 3) given disclosed concern about "material adverse effect" from loss of top customer. (2) SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION: Majority of front-end wafer fab outsourced to TSMC exclusively; assembly/test split among 5 vendors but TSMC is dual-mode. (3) CAPEX: $84.2B VMware acquisition (Nov 2023) financed with $30.4B term loans + cash. This is large-scale M&A with debt overlay. (4) DISTRIBUTOR MODEL: 48% of revenue via distributors (FY24) vs 57% (FY23) — shift toward direct OEM sales increases customer concentration risk. (5) GEOGRAPHIC CONCENTRATION: Majority inventory in Malaysia, significant Asia manufacturing footprint creates geopolitical single-point-of-failure (not extracted as risk due to boilerplate nature). (6) NO HIDDEN LEVERAGE SIGNALS detected in this excerpt — VMware debt is on-balance-sheet term loan, not SPV. (7) NO CIRCULARITY detected among Broadcom, competitors, or customers in this section. (8) NO REVENUE-ROUNDTRIP detected. (9) COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE: Large competitor set (NVIDIA, Intel, Marvell, Qualcomm, etc.) in semiconductors; software competitors include Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce, CrowdStrike in infrastructure. No direct revenue dependency on competitors. Boilerplate risk factors (IP litigation, export controls, environmental compliance, seasonality) excluded per instructions.
[chunk 2/2] This section is primarily executive biography and compensation disclosure (Item 1 Business context). No SIFI-material risks, off-balance liabilities, or counterparty concentrations are disclosed. item_1a.notes:
[chunk 2/2] AVGO 10-K (Dec 2024) risk-factor extraction. Six SIFI-material risks identified:

1. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 4): $69.85B aggregate debt load with floating-rate exposure on 2023 Term Loans — largest single financial risk disclosed.

2. COST_OPACITY (severity 3): $2.261B annual tax benefit from incentives (including Singapore) at risk as global minimum tax takes effect FY2026; this benefit is a material but fragile component of reported profitability.

3. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 3): Unquantified indemnity obligation to Dell if VMware spin-off loses tax-free status; Dell controls the audit process, removing AVGO's ability to defend its own interests.

4. EXECUTION_RISK (severity 2): VMware-heritage enterprise software customers hold termination-for-convenience rights with no penalty, creating structurally fragile recurring revenue.

5. CUSTOMER_CONCENTRATION (severity 3): Stock price and revenue explicitly tied to demand from a small set of hyperscaler customers for AI ASICs/XPUs — no specific revenue percentage disclosed but qualitatively flagged as a key driver.

6. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 3): Warranty/indemnity exposure to largest customers described as "potentially unlimited" and able to exceed revenue received — an off-income-statement contingent liability with no cap disclosed.

Skipped: generic IP litigation, ESG compliance, open-source licensing, cyber risk, product defect/recall — all real but not SIFI-material at the threshold set by the project rules.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/3] 
EXTRACTION SUMMARY — Broadcom (AVGO) 10-K FY2024 (Filed 2024-12-20)

KEY FINDINGS:

1. VMware ACQUISITION ($86.3B) — DOMINANT STRUCTURAL EVENT
   - Closed Nov 22, 2023; $30.8B cash + 544M shares ($53.4B fair value)
   - Acquired $45.6B in intangible assets, of which VCF developed technology ($24.2B) and customer contracts ($15.2B) dominate
   - PwC flagged intangible valuation as Critical Audit Matter due to subjective assumptions

2. GOODWILL + INTANGIBLES = 83.6% OF TOTAL ASSETS (COST OPACITY, Severity 3)
   - Goodwill: $97.9B (FY2024) vs $43.7B (FY2023) — more than doubled
   - Intangibles, net: $40.6B (FY2024) vs $3.9B (FY2023)
   - Total: $138.5B of $165.6B in total assets — extreme intangible concentration
   - Amortization drag: $9.27B in FY2024 ($6.0B COGS + $3.2B OpEx)

3. DEBT SURGE — HIDDEN LEVERAGE (Severity 3)
   - Long-term debt: $66.3B (FY2024) vs $37.6B (FY2023)
   - New borrowings in FY2024: $39.95B
   - Interest expense: $3.95B (FY2024) vs $1.62B (FY2023) — 144% increase
   - Total debt-to-equity: ~$67.6B debt vs $67.7B equity (≈1:1)

4. EXECUTION RISK — VMware Integration (Severity 3)
   - Restructuring charges: $254M in COGS + $1,533M in OpEx in FY2024
   - $4.7B IPR&D (mostly VCF at $4.705B) = technology not yet commercially viable at deal close

5. NO OFF-BALANCE-SHEET SPVs, VIEs, OR MATERIAL INVESTMENTS IN AI LABS identified in this section
   - No named investments in AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, etc.)
   - No SPV/JV/project-finance structures disclosed in this financial statements section
   - Operating lease policy disclosed but no specific lease concentrations or RVGs mentioned
   - Note 14 (Commitments and Contingencies) referenced but not included in source text — may contain additional purchase obligations

LIMITATIONS: Source text covers audit report, balance sheets, income statement, cash flows, equity statement, and accounting policies (Notes 1-2 only). Notes 3-14 not provided; purchase obligations, lease detail, and investment schedules likely in those notes.

[chunk 2/3] Filing: Broadcom 10-K, FY2024 (filed 2024-12-20, accession 0001730168-24-000139). Key structural findings:

1. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (severity 2): $5.9B in trade receivables sold off-balance-sheet via non-recourse factoring in FY2024 (up 60% from $3.7B in FY2022). Proceeds booked as operating cash flows — inflates OCF optics.

2. GOODWILL OPACITY (severity 3): $97.9B total goodwill, of which $54.2B was added from VMware alone in one transaction. Infrastructure Software goodwill grew 4x (from $17.6B to $71.9B). Not tax-deductible. Impairment would be catastrophic to book equity.

3. INTANGIBLE AMORTIZATION BURDEN (severity 2): $38.2B net amortizable intangibles will generate ~$8B/yr in non-cash charges for FY2025, severely depressing GAAP net income vs. cash earnings. GAAP net income was only $5.9B on $51.6B revenue — almost entirely explained by amortization drag.

4. CONTRACT LIABILITY / TERMINATION RISK (severity 2): $14.5B in contract liabilities as of Nov 2024 (vs. $2.8B prior year — 5x increase post-VMware). 55% (~$8B) subject to unilateral customer termination for convenience with pro-rata cash refund. Creates hidden liquidity risk.

5. EXECUTION RISK on VMware integration (severity 3): $2.34B IPR&D still undelivered, $54.2B goodwill contingent on synergy realization, $20.5B remaining performance obligations with 43% due in next 12 months.

6. ASIA PACIFIC CONCENTRATION (severity 2): 55% of revenue ($28.4B) from Asia Pacific, predominantly via contract manufacturers and OEM customers — geopolitical/supply chain concentration risk.

No equity investments in private AI labs or hyperscalers were disclosed in this section. No SPV/JV/VIE structures were identified beyond the factoring arrangements. Capital expenditure commitments to specific named counterparties (e.g., cloud providers, chip suppliers) were not disclosed in this section.
[chunk 3/3] Broadcom (AVGO) FY2024 10-K financial notes extraction. Key findings:

1. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (severity 3): Single unnamed semiconductor customer = 28% of FY2024 revenue ($14.4B implied). Apple is widely believed to be this customer per public reporting, but the filing does not name them — node left without named counterparty per hard rule #1.

2. CHINA CONCENTRATION (severity 3): $10.48B (~20% of revenue) shipped to China/HK in FY2024. Filing notes these may ultimately end up in US/European devices, providing partial mitigation, but geopolitical export-control risk is material.

3. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (severity 3): Total debt surged from $40.8B to $69.8B post-VMware. $13.6B is SOFR-linked floating rate, maturing 2026-2028. Debt/revenue ratio ~1.35x on $51.6B revenue. Large refinancing cliff in 2027 ($11.7B) and 2029 ($12.7B).

4. COST OPACITY — IP Transfer (severity 2): Non-recurring intra-group IP transfer drove effective tax rate to 37.8% in FY2024 (vs. 6.7% prior year). Creates $8.772B deferred tax liability. Obscures normalized earnings power.

5. COST OPACITY — Tax Cliff (severity 2): Singapore incentives ($2.26B annual benefit) expire Nov 2030; Malaysia expires FY2028. These are material to ~22% tax rate benefit. No successor arrangement disclosed.

6. No SPVs, VIEs, or off-balance-sheet entities identified in this section. No equity investments in AI labs or private companies disclosed in these notes. Operating lease restructuring charges ($277M impairments) noted but no residual value guarantees disclosed.

7. Purchase commitments ($569M) and IT service commitments ($2.77B) are modest relative to revenue and not SIFI-material on their own, but extracted for completeness.
